$description: The AI provider credentials form every gate embeds below the keyless offer: a key, a model, an endpoint, and the two buttons that keep or abandon them. Everything here is a projection — `ui/ai-credentials-form.ts` keeps the drafts, decides what a fetch is sent with, what Save actually persists and whether Cancel is on offer at all. This document never reads a setting and never calls the proxy.

style.$description: The seven `.ai-creds*` rules from `styles/shell.css`, keyed on `part` and repaired on the way. Three of them read `--spectrum-font-size-50`, which resolves only inside `<sp-theme>`; this document is mounted into a plain host inside the gate, outside that element, so each would silently have taken its hard-coded 11px fallback. The 10px column gap comes onto the kit's spacing scale at 8px.

& [part=\"title\"].$description: Centred over a left-aligned column: the form is a titled block, not a list of labelled rows.

& [part=\"note\"].$description: Where the key goes and where it does not. Quiet, because it is reassurance rather than instruction.

& [part=\"label\"].$description: The one visible heading in the column, over the field whose catalogue is fetched by the button under it.

& [part=\"key\"], & [part=\"model\"], &.$description: Every control takes the column's width; the kit's fields are inline-flex by default.

& [part=\"models-error\"].$description: Why the listing did not finish, beside the button that would try it again. Named `models-error` rather than `error` because the kit's own fields render a permanent `[part="error"]` region of their own, and a surface that reused the name would be addressing three empty paragraphs before it reached its own.

& [part=\"actions\"].$description: Buttons at the end of the column, in the order a dismissal precedes a commitment.

children.$description: One `jx-combobox` with `allows-custom-value` over the catalogue: the field IS the value, and the rows under it are what the provider happened to list. It was one `sp-combobox`, then — while the kit had no combobox — a text field and a `jx-select` bound to ONE draft, because a self-hosted id is the normal case and typing one is why the field exists. The element is built for exactly that: it filters nothing, so `options` is the catalogue as fetched; a keystroke highlights nothing, so Enter commits what was typed; and with no rows it is a text field with no chevron, which is what the form is until a listing lands. Both handlers read the ELEMENT's value, `event.currentTarget`, rather than the event target's. Not because the two ever disagree: a pick says `input` from the element, typing lets the control's own bubble, and when a listed id typed in the wrong case commits, the element has written the row's spelling to its own `value` AND to the control before the control's `change` reaches here, the runtime's bindings being synchronous — so `event.target.value` reads the same string, and no test can tell the two refs apart. `currentTarget` is read because the element is the thing whose value the form means: the ref names the contract rather than the node that happened to dispatch.

true.$description: Only offered once a key exists: with nothing stored there is nothing to go back to, and a Cancel that abandons an empty form to an empty form is a button that does nothing.
